Google annonce la fin du support de Gemi: Google announces the end of support for Gemini CLI for Google One users and free tiers starting June 18, 2025. Migration to the new Antigravity CLI platform becomes mandatory to avoid any service interruption.
Dans un mouvement stratégique visant à u: In a strategic move aimed at unifying its development tools, Google has announced the end of support for Gemini CLI for Google One users and non-paying tiers. As of June 18, 2025, this legacy version will stop responding to requests, pushing users to migrate to Antigravity CLI, a new multi-agent platform designed to centralize features.
Une transition vers une plateforme unifi: A transition to a unified platform
Gemini CLI, longtemps plébiscité pour so: Gemini CLI, long praised for its integration with development tools, is giving way to Antigravity CLI, a more modern and integrated solution. This migration is part of a rationale to simplify the tools offered by Google, particularly for developers and businesses. The new platform promises better agent management and an optimized user experience.
Pour les utilisateurs algériens, cette t: For Algerian users, this transition could have repercussions on their workflows, especially in a context where cloud development tools are gaining importance. Local businesses, often dependent on Google solutions for their digital projects, will need to anticipate this migration to avoid any service interruption.
Google a mis en place un guide de migrat: Google has set up a migration guide accessible via the link goo.gle/gemini-cli-migration. Users are invited to familiarize themselves with Antigravity CLI before the deadline to ensure a smooth transition.
Impact sur l’écosystème tech algérien: Impact on the Algerian tech ecosystem
En Algérie, où les géants des télécoms c: In Algeria, where telecom giants like Mobilis, Djezzy, and Ooredoo are increasingly relying on the cloud and digital solutions, this migration could influence the strategies of startups and local businesses. Rapid adoption of these tools could strengthen the competitiveness of the Algerian tech sector on the international stage.
